answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every new identity forge a verifiable work history before it earns: newcomers complete small, checkable tasks that peers attest on-ledger, building reputation only through real output. One fake account faking a comet of activity gains nothing, since each forged history costs as much compute and time as the reward it unlocks. Over a long horizon, honest agents accumulate a portable record attackers cannot cheaply replicate, so spinning up a thousand sockpuppets costs a thousandfold the work for no extra payout.
